title: IDWeek 2026: Viral Hemorrhagic Fever Exposure and Infection Risk in Health Care Workers - Infection Control Today

analysis.time: Advertisement IDWeek 2-26 in Washington, DC (Adobe Stock) A systematic review presented as a poster at IDWeek in Washington, DC, held from October 21 to 24, found that transmission of viral hemorrhagic fevers to health care personnel in high-income countries was rare.
analysis.event: A systematic review of 35 studies found rare transmission of viral hemorrhagic fever to health care personnel in high-income countries, highlighting the need for standardized exposure definitions.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 1,607 health care personnel exposures and 37 infections (2.3% infection rate), with no infections among laboratory personnel. Direct contact with body fluids was the most common exposure category.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The review called for standardized reporting of exposure definitions to guide risk stratification and response, with contact tracing and monitoring of exposed contacts being the most frequently reported interventions.

analysis.brief_en: A systematic review of 35 studies presented at IDWeek 2026 found that transmission of viral hemorrhagic fever to health care personnel in high-income countries is rare, with 1,607 exposures and 37 infections (2.3% infection rate). The review highlighted the need for standardized exposure definitions to guide risk assessment and response, with direct contact with body fluids being the most common exposure category.
analysis.summary_en: A systematic review of 35 studies presented at IDWeek 2026 found that transmission of viral hemorrhagic fever to health care personnel in high-income countries is rare, with 1,607 exposures and 37 infections (2.3% infection rate). The review highlighted the need for standardized exposure definitions to guide risk assessment and response, with direct contact with body fluids being the most common exposure category.

SelectScience CLINICAL24 2026 Home /News NewsClinical Diagnostics WHO emergency use listing expands access to BIOFIRE Global Fever Panel for Ebola diagnostics bioMérieux 20 Oct 2026 Summary: bioMérieux’s BIOFIRE® Global Fever Special Pathogens Panel has received World Health Organization Emergency Use Listing, expanding access to rapid differential diagnostic testing for the ongoing Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and neighbouring countries.
analysis.location_and_population: Supporting health authorities to reinforce diagnostics capabilities Since the beginning of the outbreak, bioMérieux has worked alongside Ministries of Health, public health agencies and local partners to assess diagnostic needs, strengthen laboratory capacity and support deployment of testing resources across affected regions.
analysis.event: The molecular diagnostic test can detect 16 pathogens, including multiple Ebola viruses, malaria parasites, Marburg virus, West Nile virus and Lassa virus, from a single whole blood sample in approximately one hour, helping healthcare professionals identify suspected cases, guide patient management and strengthen outbreak response.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: It enables healthcare professionals to test a single whole blood sample for 16 pathogens in approximately one hour.
